brands.d: Canonsburg, Pennsylvania inventor of roll-bonded clad cookware, founded by metallurgist John Ulam; owned by Groupe SEB since 2004.
Family-owned Villedieu-les-Poêles copper house founded by Ernest Mauviel, making copper, stainless and carbon-steel pans.

Napa Valley brand of Helen and Stanley Cheng making titanium-bonded and clad cookware developed with Michelin-starred chefs.
Morioka, Iwate foundry and the best-known Nambu tekki maker; teapots, kettles, frying pans, tamagoyaki pans and rice pots.
Oshu (Mizusawa), Iwate foundry casting bare uncoated Nambu ironware from fine-grain sand; Palma collection with Jasper Morrison.

Charleston, South Carolina maker of satin-polished, pre-seasoned skillets and carbon steel.

Japanese workshop hammering carbon-steel woks thousands of times per pan, made to order in 1.2 and 1.6 mm gauges.
Tokyo coppersmith making tin-lined copper pots and tamagoyaki pans for four generations, used by top sushi restaurants.
